item.description:

item.title: [Due in 7 days] Reminder: the Microsoft-managed 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' policy switches itself On the week of 28 October
item.description:
A tenant-wide CA policy that enforces itself is a change to sign-in behaviour nobody approved: high-risk users without a registered MFA method are blocked, and break-glass accounts are protected only if they are already excluded from the policy's group.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-28 · Open the Microsoft-managed policy in the Entra admin center now, confirm emergency-access accounts are excluded, compare its report-only results with your own risk policies, and set it On or Off deliberately before 28 October.

item.title: [Due in 7 days] A Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy, Require risk remediation for high-risk users, starts in report-only mode and switches On the week of 28 October
item.description:
From the week of 28 October a policy the tenant did not write starts deciding sign-ins for high-risk users. Emergency access accounts are not excluded automatically, and a high-risk user without a registered MFA method cannot self-remediate and is blocked, which the help desk will see before the SOC does.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-28 · Find the Microsoft-managed policy in Conditional Access now (report-only since the week of 28 September), read its report-only results in the sign-in logs, exclude break-glass accounts, confirm the users it would touch can complete MFA, and decide before 28 October whether it turns On or is set to Off.

item.description:

Graph · Add the seven names to the consent-review watch list and alert on any grant of CredentialProvenance.ReadWrite.All, HardDeletionSetting.ReadWrite.Enable or PrivilegedAccess-CustomExt.ReadWrite.All; nothing to change until an app requests them.

item.title: [New] Twelve more Graph permissions became grantable, among them UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All, which can bind a certificate to any user, and AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All
item.description:
UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All lets an application rewrite certificateUserIds, the values certificate-based authentication uses to decide which user a certificate signs in as: where certificate-based authentication is enabled, an app holding it can point a certificate issued by a CA the tenant trusts at any account, a Global Administrator included (inferred from how CBA user binding works; Microsoft's text says only that it updates certificate user IDs). It is grantable in every tenant from today and documented nowhere, so no consent review checklist names it yet.

Graph · Add the GUIDs 10d0f892-6ef8-4cd8-9f4c-614345762e90 (application) and 01d92422-30dd-4401-a504-aa0a84c463bc (delegated) of UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All and 9205f977-63a7-4c23-9d0c-8051235b0e4c / 14f19140-a110-48da-b3ba-63c2862bb7da of AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All to the consent alert list today; alert on any change to certificateUserIds in the audit log.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Deleting an Entra custom role now soft-deletes it, and Graph v1.0 can list, restore or permanently delete soft-deleted custom roles
item.description:
A deleted custom role can come back with its permissions: someone holding RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory can restore a role you removed, and a 'delete' in the audit log is no longer the end of that role.

Graph · Alert on restore and permanent delete of role definitions in the Entra audit log alongside create and update, and include soft-deleted custom roles in privileged-role reviews.

item.title: [New] Entra may now show a risk-based CAPTCHA from Arkose Labs before sending an SMS or placing a voice call for sign-in
item.description:
A user who cannot finish an SMS sign-in may be blocked by a proxy or web filter that drops the Arkose Labs domains, not by an attack. It also confirms that SMS and voice are being abused enough for Microsoft to gate them — another reason to retire them.

Entra · Add the Arkose Labs domains Microsoft lists to your proxy allow list, brief the service desk on the new dialog, and use it as a prompt to move remaining SMS and voice users to Authenticator or passkeys.

item.title: [New] Enterprise app 'Activation status' is now documented: Deactivated can mean tenant sign-in off, the app registration deactivated, or Microsoft disabling the app
item.description:
During a consent-phishing response the label 'Deactivated' is ambiguous: an analyst who sees it may assume Microsoft has already disabled the app, or may re-enable sign-in and believe the app works again. Only the three properties tell which condition applies.

Entra · Update the consent-phishing playbook to read accountEnabled, isDisabled and disabledByMicrosoftStatus through Graph instead of trusting the portal label, and alert when disabledByMicrosoftStatus is set on any service principal in your tenant.

item.title: [New] ID Protection's atypical travel detection is now documented as real-time, not offline, and the 14-day learning period is gone from the page
item.description:
A real-time detection raises sign-in risk during the sign-in itself, so a risk-based Conditional Access policy can now challenge or block an atypical-travel sign-in instead of the user being flagged after the fact. Expect more MFA prompts and blocks attributed to unlikelyTravel, and a change in DetectionTimingType in AADUserRiskEvents.

Entra · Review sign-in-risk Conditional Access policies with this in mind, tell the service desk that travelling users may be challenged at sign-in, and trend unlikelyTravel by DetectionTimingType to see when your tenant moves (query in Hunting).

item.title: [New] October security update switches NTLMv1-derived SSO credentials from audit to block on devices without Credential Guard
item.description:
A wave of Wi-Fi or VPN failures after Patch Tuesday will look like an outage or a credential attack. The temporary fix, BlockNtlmv1SSO = 0, re-enables a weak credential path; anyone who sets it fleet-wide without an expiry undoes the hardening.

Windows · Inventory 802.1X and VPN profiles that still use PEAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-MSCHAPv2 on Windows 11 24H2+ and Server 2025 without Credential Guard; plan the move to EAP-TLS; if you must return devices to audit mode, scope it by group, record an end date and watch Event ID 4024 until it stops.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: [New] From 4 November every default user can create agent blueprints unless 'Users can create agent blueprints' is set to No
item.description:
A default-on permission for every member user to create a new kind of workload identity widens the app-registration surface that consent-phishing and persistence techniques already abuse, and tenants that locked down app registration are not covered by that setting.

Entra · Decide before 4 November: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No unless there is a business case, keep Agent ID Developer as the delegated path, and add agent blueprint creation by non-admins to the app-registration detections.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Entra stops auto-granting AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprints from 4 November; app-only agents that create their own identities need explicit admin consent or get 403
item.description:
Until now every agent blueprint could mint agent identities without any admin approval and without a visible grant. After the change that authority becomes an auditable, revocable app-role assignment, so the grant itself becomes something to monitor.

Entra · Before 4 November, filter the Entra audit log on ApplicationManagement / Add Service Principal where the initiator is an Application and the target an agent identity; grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager explicitly (from 16 October) only to the blueprints that need it, and alert on new grants of it afterwards.

item.title: [New] Entra Kerberos gets one configuration guide: the key-rotation page is folded into it, with a stated rotation practice and a warning that only Set-AzureADKerberosServer may rotate the key
item.description:
A trust whose direction was described backwards gets reviewed backwards: the Trusted Domain Object is an object in AD DS that lets Entra ID accept AD-issued referrals, and tenants that only need Windows Hello cloud Kerberos trust or FIDO2 do not need it at all.

Entra · Check whether a KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM Trusted Domain Object exists in each forest (Get-ADTrust), keep it only where Azure Files or SQL MI need it, and treat it as a tier-0 object in AD monitoring.
